- speckit-converge: Assess the current codebase against the feature's spec, plan, and tasks, then append any remaining unbuilt work as new tasks to tasks.md so implement can complete it.

- speckit-plan: Execute the implementation planning workflow using the plan template to generate design artifacts.
- speckit-specify: Create or update the feature specification from a natural language feature description.
- speckit-tasks: Generate an actionable, dependency-ordered tasks.md for the feature based on available design artifacts.
- speckit-taskstoissues: Convert existing tasks into actionable, dependency-ordered GitHub issues for the feature based on available design artifacts.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them.   that a caller cannot reach it alone. **A session with it switched off is bounded
  by nothing time-based at all**, and the four constraints around this one are
  then the whole of the containment. That is a state an operator may choose; it is
  not a state anything here prevents.

  *Amended 2.0.0: an idle timeout was required here until 2026-08-14. It was
  withdrawn because it bounded the wrong thing — a session waiting for a human is
  quiet, and destroying it for that lost work the operator expected to keep — not
  because it was mis-measured. What it cost to remove is written above.*
- Teardown is **verified**, not assumed. An orphaned tmux window is a live
  unsandboxed shell with no owner.
- The listener binds **loopback only**. Reachability comes from the tunnel.

A feature that widens any of these needs an explicit justification in the plan
naming what now becomes reachable.

### VII. Design system is binding

[`docs/design-system.md`](../../docs/design-system.md) and
[`docs/components.md`](../../docs/components.md) define the vocabulary for the
dashboard.

- Tokens only — never a hard-coded colour, size, or font in a template.
- Reuse the canonical component. A second session card is a defect.
- **Pane output is rendered as text, never as HTML.** Everything a Claude session
  prints reaches the browser. This is the project's only XSS surface and it is
  closed by construction, not by sanitising.

---

## Development Workflow

Three lanes, one set of rules. All inherit these principles.

| Lane | When | Path |
|---|---|---|
| **Feature** | More than one moving part | constitution → `/speckit-specify` → `/speckit-plan` → `/speckit-tasks` → `/speckit-implement` |
| **Quick fix** | One-line bug, typo, copy | Fix → verify → one line in `docs/fixes-log.md` |
| **Automated** | Issue labelled `claude-fix` | Runner → bounded run → **PR only, never `main`** |

Autonomous execution (`ralph/loop.sh`) works the plan **one task per iteration**
with a fresh context each time, and commits after each. It is bound by every
principle above.

---

## Quality Gates

A change may merge only when all of these are true:

- [ ] Build, test, and lint green (the `AGENTS.md` commands)
- [ ] New behaviour has a test that fails without the change
- [ ] `docs/security.md` checklist satisfied for anything touching input, authz, or secrets
- [ ] `docs/auth-and-sessions.md` checklist satisfied, if auth or the session lifecycle was touched
- [ ] Cross-session isolation still holds; teardown still verified
- [ ] `docs/design-system.md` + `docs/components.md` respected for anything visual
- [ ] No `NEEDS CLARIFICATION` left unanswered
- [ ] Reviewed by a code owner (`.github/CODEOWNERS`)

---

## Governance

This constitution supersedes all other practice. Amending it requires a pull
request that states what changed, why, and what it breaks — reviewed by a code
owner like any other change.

Complexity must be justified in the plan. "It might be useful later" is not a
justification.

Agents: `AGENTS.md` is your runtime guide; this document is the authority behind it.

# Go Conventions

> Loaded when: writing or changing any Go in this repo.
> `AGENTS.md` states these rules; this file shows them.

## Naming

Standard Go. Packages lowercase and singular; no `util`, no `common` — a package
named for what it contains rather than what it does becomes a drawer.

```go
package session       // files: manager.go, manager_test.go
func (m *Manager) Create(ctx context.Context, req CreateRequest) (*Session, error)
```

## Errors

Never swallow one. Wrap with `%w` and context; return, do not log-and-continue.

```go
if err := m.tmux.Kill(ctx, s.Target()); err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("kill session %s: %w", s.ID, err)  // never a bare `return err`
}
```

Sentinel errors for conditions a caller branches on (`ErrSessionNotFound`), checked
with `errors.Is` rather than by string.

**Never put a secret, a prompt, or pane content in an error string.** Errors travel
to logs, and `docs/security.md` §3 makes all three secret. A bare `return err` from a
package that touched the host is how tmux's own stderr ends up in the audit trail.

## Tests

Table-driven, `t.Parallel()`, no network, no real tmux — `tmuxctl.Controller` is an
interface with a fake, and the fake records exact argv so a test can assert no shell
string was ever built.

Every PR needs a test that fails without the change. Auth and session code also needs
the **negative** cases: bad signature, stale timestamp, replay, wrong owner.

```go
req := signedRequest(t, a, `{"cwd":"/repo"}`)
mustVerify(t, a, req)                            // first use passes
if _, err := a.Verify(clone(t, req)); err == nil {
    t.Fatal("replayed request was accepted")     // this is the whole point
}
```

Tests that need a real tmux or a real binary live behind a build tag — `//go:build
tmux` for the integration suite, `//go:build quickstart` for an acceptance run — so
that `go test ./...` stays fast and hermetic. Both are in the command table in
`AGENTS.md`; neither runs by default.

**A test that cannot fail is not a test.** Three defects in this repo shipped with
full green suites. Two because the thing under test had no production caller: the
reaper, and the idle clock. The third because the fake agreed with the daemon
about a field neither of them carried — the session lifetime was written to no
tmux option and read back from none, and every adoption test passed while a
never-expiring session came back mortal. Assert the caller, not only the callee,
and make the fake hold what the host holds.

## Comments

Explain *why*, never *what*. If the code needs a "what" comment, rewrite the code.

The comments worth writing are the ones that stop a later reader "fixing" something
correct. This repo has several — `path` vs `PATH` in a zsh function, `=name` vs
`=name:` for a tmux target, `alg` read only to reject — and each exists because
somebody lost time to it once.

578	## The session journal (the one file this daemon writes)
579	
580	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crswd/sessions-.jsonl`, else `~/.config/crswd/sessions-.jsonl`.
581	It is the only durable state the daemon keeps, and it exists because the host
582	stopped being sufficient: on 2026-08-22 the kernel OOM killer took a whole
583	`tmux-spawn` cgroup and destroyed a session's tmux state along with it, so
584	everything recorded on that tmux session went too.
585	
586	**What it holds**: session id, owner, session name, conversation identifier,
587	working directory, start-command *name*, lifetime, original creation time, and a
588	revival attempt count. That is the set the daemon cannot rediscover once the
589	shell is gone. The session name is caller-supplied but not free text:
590	`ValidateName` holds it to `^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,64}$` before it is a session's, and a
591	revival cannot render its start command without it.
592	
593	**What it must never hold**: a bearer token, a token hash, pane content,
594	conversation content, or caller-supplied free text. The rule FR-042 places on the
595	audit trail applies here unchanged — there is simply no request behind this file.
596	A start-command *name* is recorded and a command *line* never is: a stored
597	command line would be a command line a restart could be made to run.
598	
599	**Mode `0600`**, created with the directory at `0700`.
600	
601	**One journal per daemon, named after its listen address** — the same thing the
602	tmux server is named after (`tmuxctl.SocketFor`). Two daemons on one host must not
603	replay each other's sessions any more than they may see each other's shells, and
604	without this they do: a second daemon sharing a home directory replays the first
605	one's journal, finds those sessions absent from its *own* tmux server, and stands
606	ready to recreate every one of them on it.
607	
608	**Append-only, fsynced per record.** The failure being defended against is an
609	unclean stop, and a rewritten document degrades to a truncated file where a log
610	degrades to a missing last line. On this host the unclean reset of 2026-08-17
611	lost a flag out of a rewritten `~/.claude.json` and took a gitignored `.env` with
612	it — that is the failure mode, observed, on this machine.
613	
614	**Reading it is fail-loud, replaying it is fail-safe.** A missing file means no
615	session has been created yet. An unreadable one is fatal at startup, because a
616	daemon that continued would supervise nothing and report nothing. A torn final
617	line is discarded and counted. And every replayed candidate is re-checked against
618	the allowlist, the ceiling and the cap in force *now* — a journal outlives the
619	configuration that produced it, and it must never reinstate a session the
620	operator's current configuration would refuse to create.

687	## Rate limiting & audit
688	
689	- Per-caller rate limit on session creation. Spawning Claude sessions is expensive
690	  and unbounded spawning is a local denial of service. **Both doors create**, so the
691	  browser's create calls the same limiter and the same validation rather than a second
692	  copy of either.
693	- Per-source rate limit on `POST /login`, on **the same token bucket**, which is generic
694	  over its key rather than duplicated: a create's budget is spent by an identity because
695	  it sits behind layer 2, and a sign-in's is spent by an address because establishing an
696	  identity is what it is for. The type parameter is what keeps one from being spent by
697	  the other's key. Two limiters over two copies of the bucket would be two rules about
698	  what a budget is, free to disagree.
699	- **What that limiter remembers is bounded by its own sweep**, and since the sign-in
700	  budget exists that is load-bearing: its keys are addresses a stranger chooses, so what
701	  keeps the map small is that every decision drops every bucket that has refilled to the
702	  top — an entry survives only while it is partly spent.
703	- Cap concurrent sessions; refuse past the cap rather than degrading the host.
704	- **Every request is audited**: timestamp, caller ID, action, session ID, decision.
705	  Audit records carry no prompt text and no session output.

710	  alarming event than one that never got in, and an operator counting one must not be
711	  counting the other with it.
712	- **What was delivered is never recorded.** The compact's own text is a constant the
713	  daemon sends into a session; the record says the action happened, never its content.

715	  never carry a byte the caller chose.
716	
717	## Pre-merge security checklist
718	
719	- [ ] No secret added to the repo (CI + push protection verify this)
720	- [ ] Every new endpoint enforces authn **and** ownership server-side

722	      existed, returns 404 and not 403 — the 403 is the action gate's answer to a
723	      request it would not accept at all, and the two never stand in for each other

733	- [ ] A new setting a secret could be written into is classified by `config.IsSecret`,

The browser's credential is an ambient cookie, so "the operator's identity was verified" and "the operator asked for this" are different facts; the second is what the action gate establishes. A session is `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`; a credential in its environment is one `env` away from being pane content, and pane content on this product travels into model context and a transcript that leaves the host. Fail closed Any error in the auth path denies the request. A missing config value that would weaken auth is a **startup failure**, not a warning: ```go if cfg.SharedSecret == "" { return fmt.Errorf("CRSW_SHARED_SECRET is required; refusing to start") } ``` A daemon that starts with auth disabled is worse than one that does not start. The probe reads the *configured* commands rather than a fixed `claude`, **installs nothing, and never runs what it found**. A daemon that installs software is a daemon that can be made to install software, and one that executed a probed binary to see whether it works would be running an operator's command line at startup with no session to run it in. It does run **one** thing, and the bounds on it are the whole of why that is allowed. A start command is resolved inside a tmux pane's login shell, so a probe asking only this process's `PATH` warns about commands that work — and a check that is wrong about a healthy host trains an operator to ignore it. The trade this takes is real and named here rather than buried: the daemon now executes a file it does not own (`~/.profile`) at startup. It is taken because the alternative was a check that lies, and it is bounded by every line above. ### 5. Dependencies - Dependabot is enabled. Security updates merge promptly, not eventually. - A new dependency needs justification: what does it do that stdlib cannot? The HTTP server, HMAC, and JSON handling are all stdlib. Keep it that way. - **`go.sum` must not exist**, and that is asserted by a test in the default build rather than remembered. It is the reason the configuration file is `key = value` hand-parsed: YAML and TOML have no standard-library parser, neither is safe to hand-roll, and a dependency for either would create the file this rule forbids. - **The rule covers the host module**, the root `go.mod` that builds the VM daemon and every release. Everything it supplies goes through exactly the loader an environment variable goes through, so no bound, default or refusal is written twice and a value cannot mean one thing in a unit and another in a file. **Precedence is flag → environment → file → default**, decided in one shim. The order is the security property: reversed, a stale file on a host silently overrides the environment a container was configured with. A daemon with no file therefore behaves exactly as one built before the file existed, which is what makes the change safe to deploy at all. **Nothing in the daemon writes the operator's file.** `crswd config migrate` is the only code in this repository that writes a configuration file, and it is a command the operator runs. `GET /settings` renders that resolved configuration, and it is the one page holding every secret at render time: - **A secret's value is `present` or `absent` and nothing else.** Not a length, not a prefix, not a suffix, not a hash. A masked value is still a disclosure, and the four characters of a credential a page is willing to print are four an attacker no longer has to guess. The word is chosen in Go by `config.IsSecret` and reaches the template already decided, so there is no raw value beside it for a later render to reach for. - **The source column is recorded, never inferred.** The shim writes it as it decides. A file and an environment holding the same bytes are indistinguishable by comparison, and that is exactly the case an operator is on the page to ask about. - **No mutating verb is registered on `/settings` at all.** Not a route that refuses — no route. Writing the operator's configuration file from a browser is the highest-consequence surface in the product; a route that does not exist cannot be exploited, mis-gated, or reached by a refactor that forgets which door it is on. **Sweep every route for secrets, do not reason about it.** The check that matters is the absence of a value across every registered path on both doors, asserted the way the `Access-Control-Allow-*` absence below is. ## Transport & exposure The daemon binds **loopback by default**, and the deployment this was written for is not reachable any other way: a Cloudflare Tunnel connects outbound and brokers `*.example.com` traffic to the loopback listener, and no inbound port is opened on the host or the router. ``` internet → Cloudflare edge (TLS, Access) → tunnel (outbound) → 127.0.0.1:PORT ``` Since M12 there is a second one — an operator on their own network with no Cloudflare in front of this daemon at all, reaching it from the machine they are sitting at: ``` operator's browser → LAN → 0.0.0.0:PORT ``` **The invariant is "never reachable without authentication", not "never reachable".** That is the whole of what the bind rule now says, and it is a bound relaxed rather than deleted: - A non-loopback address is permitted **only when layer 1 admits somebody** — an Access door or a dashboard password. A daemon whose dashboard admits nobody (`closedDoor`, which is what a daemon with neither has) refuses to bind off loopback, and the refusal is a **startup failure**, not a warning. - It is checked in the three places the loopback rule was always checked: `config.loadListen` on the configured value, `httpapi.assertBindAddress` on the configured string again, and `httpapi.assertBoundAddress` on the address the kernel actually handed back — the only one of the three that is evidence rather than intent. The second asks both what was configured *and* which layer 1 was wired, because a daemon whose file names a door it did not build is a wiring defect and must not be what puts a listener on the network. - A host **name** is refused under every door. `/etc/hosts` or a resolver can point `localhost` anywhere, so only an IP literal says where the listener will be. - The development bypass is not a door. It authenticates nobody, configures no door, and `internal/access` refuses a non-loopback listener under it besides. If a change would let a daemon that admits nobody listen on `0.0.0.0`, that change is wrong. ### Response headers Every **browser-door** response carries all of these — pages, static assets, refusals, and the not-found page alike. A refusal that carried a different set would be a refusal that tells a stranger which paths this daemon really serves: | Header | Value | |---|---| | `Content-Security-Policy` | `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'` | | `Strict-Transport-Security` | `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` | | `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff` | | `Referrer-Policy` | `no-referrer` | | `Cache-Control` | `no-store` — with exactly one exemption, below | No `unsafe-inline`, no CDN. The stylesheet and the dashboard's script are served from `self`, embedded in the binary via `go:embed`; a client-side library would be too, and never from a CDN. If a change needs `unsafe-inline` to work, the change is wrong. `no-store` is the default rather than the exception, because a page, a stream, and an authorisation decision are all things a cached copy outlives: pages carry session names, working directories, and pane content, all secret under §3. **The two embedded static assets are the only exemption** — they hold no session data, and they are served `no-cache` with an entity tag rather than a lifetime, so a browser revalidates instead of running the previous binary's script against this one's markup. The API door's responses gain none of these headers. Every byte a milestone 1 client sees is frozen, and a header is part of a response. ### The header that must never appear | Header | Rule | |---|---| | `Access-Control-Allow-*` | **Never sent. Any of them, on any route, on either door.** | This is load-bearing, not hygiene. The browser's credential is a cookie and therefore **ambient**: it rides on requests a hostile third-party page triggers, and the edge converts those into a valid assertion the daemon accepts. Same-origin policy is the only thing stopping that page from *reading* the response, and it holds exactly as long as the daemon never opts out of it. The per-session bearer token would have provided this a second way — a header credential forces a preflight, a cookie does not — but a browser stream cannot carry one, so the absence *is* the protection. **Assert the absence.** Sweep every registered route on both doors and require zero such headers. An absence nothing checks is one convenience header away from gone, and there is deliberately no CORS helper in the codebase to reach for. The request side of the same rule: a live output stream is refused when the browser itself reports a cross-site initiator — `Sec-Fetch-Site` present and anything other than `same-origin`. **Present-and-wrong refuses; absent does not**: browsers send the header and non-browser clients do not, so requiring it would refuse the callers it was never about while adding nothing against the one it is. The refusal is decided before any session is looked up, and the header's value is caller-authored text that never reaches a log line or an audit record. **On a route that changes something, absent refuses too.** Same check, same code, one addition — and the difference is the argument above running out. The only legitimate caller of an action route is a form this daemon rendered, submitted by a browser, which always sends the header; a script that wants to change something uses the API door and its signature. An absent header is not evidence of same-origin initiation, and treating it as such makes the check optional for anything that can omit it. It is still only half the defence: the other half is the page token, because a header a future proxy could strip must not be the whole of it. ## Rendering session output (the one XSS surface) Everything a Claude session prints — file contents, command output, error text, a web page it fetched — reaches the dashboard. **All of it is untrusted.** ```go // html/template escapes by default. Keep pane output as a plain string and let // the template engine do its job. {{ .PaneText }} // correct: escaped text node {{ .PaneText | safeHTML }} // NEVER. There is no valid reason for this. ``` - Never `template.HTML`, `template.JS`, or any `safeHTML`-style helper on pane content. Not for ANSI colour, not for links, not for formatting. - On the client, `textContent` only. Never `innerHTML`, never `hx-swap` a raw pane payload into the DOM as markup — stream it into a `
` as text.
- Strip ANSI escape sequences server-side before rendering. If colour is wanted
  later, map codes to CSS classes from an allowlist; never pass the raw bytes through.
- The same applies to session names and working directories. A caller picks those,
  and the regex in §2 is what keeps them boring.

## The session journal (the one file this daemon writes)

`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crswd/sessions-.jsonl`, else `~/.config/crswd/sessions-.jsonl`.
It is the only durable state the daemon keeps, and it exists because the host
stopped being sufficient: on 2026-08-22 the kernel OOM killer took a whole
`tmux-spawn` cgroup and destroyed a session's tmux state along with it, so
everything recorded on that tmux session went too.

**What it holds**: session id, owner, session name, conversation identifier,
working directory, start-command *name*, lifetime, original creation time, and a
revival attempt count. That is the set the daemon cannot rediscover once the
shell is gone. The session name is caller-supplied but not free text:
`ValidateName` holds it to `^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,64}$` before it is a session's, and a
revival cannot render its start command without it.

**What it must never hold**: a bearer token, a token hash, pane content,
conversation content, or caller-supplied free text. The rule FR-042 places on the
audit trail applies here unchanged — there is simply no request behind this file.
A start-command *name* is recorded and a command *line* never is: a stored
command line would be a command line a restart could be made to run.

**Mode `0600`**, created with the directory at `0700`.

**One journal per daemon, named after its listen address** — the same thing the
tmux server is named after (`tmuxctl.SocketFor`). Two daemons on one host must not
replay each other's sessions any more than they may see each other's shells, and
without this they do: a second daemon sharing a home directory replays the first
one's journal, finds those sessions absent from its *own* tmux server, and stands
ready to recreate every one of them on it.

**Append-only, fsynced per record.** The failure being defended against is an
unclean stop, and a rewritten document degrades to a truncated file where a log
degrades to a missing last line. On this host the unclean reset of 2026-08-17
lost a flag out of a rewritten `~/.claude.json` and took a gitignored `.env` with
it — that is the failure mode, observed, on this machine.

**Reading it is fail-loud, replaying it is fail-safe.** A missing file means no
session has been created yet. An unreadable one is fatal at startup, because a
daemon that continued would supervise nothing and report nothing. A torn final
line is discarded and counted. And every replayed candidate is re-checked against
the allowlist, the ceiling and the cap in force *now* — a journal outlives the
configuration that produced it, and it must never reinstate a session the
operator's current configuration would refuse to create.

## Claude Code's workspace trust (a file this daemon edits but does not own)

Before typing a start command, the daemon sets
`projects[].hasTrustDialogAccepted` to `true` in the `.claude.json` a
session will read (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `$HOME`, from the session's own
environment). Without it a session in a never-trusted directory sits on Claude
Code's trust dialog with nobody to answer it (`internal/session/trust.go`).

**This grants nothing `allowed_roots` did not.** Only a directory `ResolveWorkDir`
accepted reaches it, and a session there already runs with tool approval off.

**It edits someone else's file, so it touches as little as it can.** An
already-trusted directory is read and not rewritten. A missing file stays
missing. A rewrite takes the `.lock` flock ai-lawnmower's `trust-seed.sh`
takes, carries every other value through as raw JSON, and replaces the file by
rename. A file that is not a JSON object fails the create rather than being
repaired. Wired only in `httpapi.New`, so no test server reaches the operator's
real file. Not wired in kubernetes mode.

### Codex's workspace trust (amendment, spec 019 D10)

For a Codex session the same step seeds a `[projects.""]` table holding
`trust_level = "trusted"` in `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` (else `$HOME/.codex`), from the
session's own environment (`internal/session/trust_codex.go`). Everything above holds: it
grants nothing `allowed_roots` did not, an already-trusted directory is not rewritten, a
rewrite takes the `.lock` flock and replaces the file by rename, and it is wired only in
`httpapi.New`.

- **No TOML library.** The root module has no dependencies (section 5). The edit is line-level
  and understands exactly the shape Codex writes itself: that header line and a `trust_level`
  line in the table. Any other mention of the directory refuses the create rather than being
  edited.
- **A missing `config.toml` is created at 0600** when `$CODEX_HOME` exists, because Codex's own
  trust acceptance creates the same table in the same file. A missing `$CODEX_HOME` stays
  missing: Codex has never run there.
- **The trust level is never passed with `-c` on the command line.** That would put a
  caller-influenced path into a line typed at a shell, and no line this daemon types carries one.

### Codex conversation listing (amendment to spec 013 FR-025, spec 019 D11)

FR-025 says a transcript is never opened, because Claude's file name is the id and its
directory is the working directory. Codex keys rollouts by date and the working directory
exists only inside line 1, so listing a Codex directory's conversations opens each rollout
**once, bounded**: at most 64 KiB read, stopping at the first newline, decoding only `type`,
`payload.id` and `payload.cwd`. Nothing it reads is rendered or logged. It scans at most 500
rollout files, newest date directory first, and returns at most 50 matches. Claude's listing
still opens nothing.

### Codex's update check (spec 019 D5)

Codex checks for a new release on startup and offers to install it. A line typed into a pane
can answer that offer, so an update prompt is a way for typed input to install software. The
daemon therefore adds `-c check_for_update_on_startup=false` to every Codex line it types
(and `--no-alt-screen`, without which tmux keeps no scrollback), and configuration refuses a
Codex command that sets the check back to true. It is a daemon-owned flag, not an operator
choice, because a forgotten flag costs a global package install.

### Codex's dangerous flags are the operator's

`--dangerously-skip-permissions` is the operator's choice for Claude Code, and for Codex the
equivalents are `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (no approval prompts, no sandbox)
and `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` (hooks run without review). The daemon adds neither.
Put them in the `codex` entry of `start_commands` if you want unattended sessions, with the
same consequences as for Claude: a request that passes auth runs code on this host unsandboxed.

## Rate limiting & audit

- Per-caller rate limit on session creation. Spawning Claude sessions is expensive
  and unbounded spawning is a local denial of service. **Both doors create**, so the
  browser's create calls the same limiter and the same validation rather than a second
  copy of either.
- Per-source rate limit on `POST /login`, on **the same token bucket**, which is generic
  over its key rather than duplicated: a create's budget is spent by an identity because
  it sits behind layer 2, and a sign-in's is spent by an address because establishing an
  identity is what it is for. The type parameter is what keeps one from being spent by
  the other's key. Two limiters over two copies of the bucket would be two rules about
  what a budget is, free to disagree.
- **What that limiter remembers is bounded by its own sweep**, and since the sign-in
  budget exists that is load-bearing: its keys are addresses a stranger chooses, so what
  keeps the map small is that every decision drops every bucket that has refilled to the
  top — an entry survives only while it is partly spent.
- Cap concurrent sessions; refuse past the cap rather than degrading the host.
- **Every request is audited**: timestamp, caller ID, action, session ID, decision.
  Audit records carry no prompt text and no session output.
- A browser action is audited under its own name — `dashboard.create`,
  `dashboard.destroy`, `dashboard.rename`, `dashboard.compact` — and a request the
  action gate refused under `dashboard.reject`, deliberately not `access.reject`: an
  identity that got in and *then* failed the cross-site check is a different and more
  alarming event than one that never got in, and an operator counting one must not be
  counting the other with it.
- **What was delivered is never recorded.** The compact's own text is a constant the
  daemon sends into a session; the record says the action happened, never its content.
  Every reason on the trail is a sentinel this codebase authored, so a record can
  never carry a byte the caller chose.

## Pre-merge security checklist

- [ ] No secret added to the repo (CI + push protection verify this)
- [ ] Every new endpoint enforces authn **and** ownership server-side
- [ ] Session IDs unguessable; a session another caller owns, or one that never
      existed, returns 404 and not 403 — the 403 is the action gate's answer to a
      request it would not accept at all, and the two never stand in for each other
- [ ] Any new mutating browser route goes through the action gate, not just layer 1,
      and both halves of that gate are tested with the other satisfied
- [ ] Input decoded into a typed struct with unknown fields rejected
- [ ] No shell string built; `exec.Command` with argv only
- [ ] Any caller-supplied path allowlisted and symlink-resolved
- [ ] Auth failures are uniform and leak no detail about which check failed
- [ ] No session output, prompt, or token in any log line
- [ ] Listener still bound to loopback, or bound wider only on a daemon whose
      layer 1 admits somebody
- [ ] A new setting a secret could be written into is classified by `config.IsSecret`,
      so the 0600 refusal and the settings page cannot disagree about it
- [ ] No secret value on any rendered page — swept across every route, not reasoned about
- [ ] No new dependency without justification, and the root `go.sum` still absent
- [ ] No `Access-Control-Allow-*` on any route, either door — swept, not assumed
- [ ] Browser-door responses all carry the header set above, refusals included

changes. The spec lives at `specs/020-prompt-route-safety/` because 018 and 019 are
already taken here.

## Conventions

  says how to prove it.

## Decisions already made (copy these into research.md; do not reopen them)

- **D1 Spec number.** `specs/020-prompt-route-safety`. 018 is interactive-input, 019 is codex-runtime.
- **D2 Liveness gate (req 1).** Probe check 13: `@crswd-binary` matched `pane_current_command`
  (`claude`) on 6 of 6 live panes, 3 of them `rcq`. The gate reads the session's row from the
  controller's `List` and its `Claude` liveness. `LivenessStopped` refuses. `LivenessUnknown`
  passes, as spec 012 FR-006 reads it. It runs before the paste and again after the paste; if
  the second read is stopped, the daemon sends `C-u` and no Enter. No new `Controller` method,
  so the k8s module's `podctl` is untouched.
- **D3 Not-ready answer (reqs 1, 2, 5).** One sentinel `session.ErrSessionNotReady`. The prompt
  handler maps it to `409` with body `{"error":"session not ready"}` and an audit Deny with reason
  `session not ready`. A `failed` session gets it. `dead` stays as it is today.
- **D4 Bracketed paste (req 3).** `Manager.Prompt` uses `PasteBracketed` for every harness.
  `Manager.Compact` keeps its harness-based paste. No newline refusal: the opp-lease handoff
  pastes multi-line item bodies.
- **D5 Leading `!` or `/` (req 4).** API door only. Refuse when the first character that is not
  space, tab, CR or LF is `!` or `/`: `400` with the uniform bad-request body, before any tmux
  command. Grep of 10/14/26: lawnmower's callers (`console.py` `_answer_action` via

  `opp_followup_prompt`) all start with a letter. The browser type route is unchanged. This

# Research: prompt route safety

**Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) · **Plan**: [plan.md](plan.md) · **Tasks**: [tasks.md](tasks.md)

The requirements come from `~/code/ai-lawnmower/docs/mcp-session-steering-design.md`,
section (g) "Phase 3 detail", and the evidence from the probe run recorded in
`~/code/ai-lawnmower/ralph/plans/lm-steer-design/results.md`. Both live outside this
repository and are read, never edited. Everything cited below as a *probe check* is a
numbered check in that results file; everything cited as *measured here* was read off
this tree on 10/14/26 and is restated in `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/PROGRESS.md`
so a later iteration need not re-measure it.

The decisions were taken before the plan was cut. They are recorded here in full so the
spec, the plan and the task list all cite one source. **They are not reopened by this
spec** — a decision that needs changing needs a new one, with its own evidence.

## D1 — Spec number

The spec lives at `specs/020-prompt-route-safety/`.

The design calls this work "crswd spec 018". That number is taken here: `specs/018-interactive-input`
is the session page's input panel and `specs/019-codex-runtime` is the Codex runtime
(measured here: both directories exist and carry a `spec.md`). The next free number is 020.

*Rejected: reusing 018 because the design names it.* A spec directory is addressed by
number from `tasks.md`, from `docs/`, and from the two specs that this one amends; two
specs under one number is a reference that resolves to the wrong document.

## D2 — Liveness gate (requirement 1)

`Manager.Prompt` reads the session's row out of the controller's `List` and consults its
`Claude` liveness before it pastes, and again after the paste:

- `LivenessStopped` returns `ErrSessionNotReady` and nothing is typed.
- `LivenessUnknown` delivers. That is the reading `tmuxctl.Liveness` documents for
  every caller — it is the zero value precisely so that a caller who forgets the field
  reads "alive" — and it is how spec 012's detection requirement (FR-006) is already
  satisfied in `internal/session/supervisor.go`: an unknown liveness is a session
  started before `@crswd-binary` existed, not evidence of a stopped harness.
- A failing `List` is an error, not a pass. The gate fails closed.
- If the *second* read is stopped — Claude exited between the paste and the submit — the
  daemon sends `C-u` and no Enter, so the half-delivered text is cleared off the shell's
  line rather than executed by it, and the call still answers `ErrSessionNotReady`.

Evidence: probe check 13 — the `@crswd-binary` tmux option matched `pane_current_command`
(`claude`) on 6 of 6 live panes, 3 of them under `rcq`. So the option this daemon already
sets is a usable liveness answer on the panes lawnmower actually drives, and the gate
needs no new fact on the host.

Measured here: the fake controller's `List` already derives `Claude` liveness from
`@crswd-binary` against the pane command (`livenessOf`), and the fake has
`SetPaneCommand(name, command)` to drive it.

*Rejected: a per-session liveness method on `tmuxctl.Controller`.* There is none today,
and the interface has a second implementation — `k8s/internal/podctl` — which a seventh
method would force to change. `k8s/` is out of this milestone's reach by construction, so
the gate reads the row it can already get.

*Rejected: trusting the stored session state alone.* A pane whose harness exited is still
`running` in the store until the next supervisor sweep; the whole point of the gate is to
answer for the pane as it is at the moment of the paste.

## D3 — Not-ready answer (requirements 1, 2, 5)

One sentinel, `session.ErrSessionNotReady`, carries every "the session cannot take a
prompt right now" refusal. The prompt handler maps it to `409` with body
`{"error":"session not ready"}` and records an audit Deny whose reason is the sentinel's
text, `session not ready`.

A session in state `failed` is refused with it before any tmux command runs. `dead` keeps
the answer it gives today (`ErrSessionDead`), because that is a frozen client-visible
behaviour and nothing in this spec asks to change it.

Evidence: lawnmower's `deliver()` (`~/code/ai-lawnmower/loop/session_resume.py`) already
treats any response body carrying an `error` key as a refusal, so a 409 of this shape
reads as a refusal to the only caller this route has today without a change on that side.

One sentinel rather than three keeps the refusal uniform: the caller learns that the
session is not ready and not *which* of the gates said so. The three are distinguished
only server-side, on the trail.

## D4 — Bracketed paste (requirement 3)

`Manager.Prompt` pastes with `PasteBracketed` for every harness. `Manager.Compact` keeps
its harness-based paste and is untouched.

Evidence: spec 019 M3/M4 measured that a plain `paste-buffer -d` plus Enter does not
submit on Codex while `paste-buffer -p -d` plus Enter does, for one line and for two;
spec 018 added `Controller.PasteBracketed` and spec 019 D9 left "whether Claude moves to
bracketed paste too" to spec 018's successor. This is that decision, and it is taken for
both harnesses so that one route has one delivery shape. Spec 018 FR-006 reads "plain
paste, then Enter. Bracketed paste is for the interactive route only", so **this decision
amends that FR** as well as D5 does; the amendment is recorded in spec.md. Bracketed paste is also what makes the C0 refusal
in `docs/security.md` §2 load-bearing rather than decorative: inside a bracketed paste a
literal `ESC[201~` would end the paste, and that text is already refused.

**No newline refusal.** The opp-lease handoff pastes multi-line item bodies (the fixtures
in `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/PROGRESS.md` are multi-line as lawnmower builds them
today), so refusing `\n` would refuse the traffic this route exists to carry.

Measured here: `m.paste` is bracketed only when the harness spec says `BracketedPaste`,
which Claude's does not — so this is a behaviour change for Claude sessions and needs the
failing-before test that proves it.

## D5 — A leading `!` or `/` is refused (requirement 4)

On the **API door only**, a prompt is refused when the first character that is not a
space, a tab, a CR or an LF is `!` or `/`: `400` with the uniform bad-request body,
before any tmux command runs.

`/` opens a Claude Code slash command and `!` opens its shell escape. A caller that can
reach this route can already run code on the host through a session, so this is not a
containment boundary; it is a refusal of the two prefixes that make a *delivered prompt*
mean something other than a prompt — a steering message that silently became `/clear` is
a lost conversation with no error anywhere.

Evidence: a grep of lawnmower's callers on 10/14/26 — `console.py` `_answer_action` (via
`session_resume.deliver`), `lawnmower-route` `resume_prompt`, `_batch_listing_prompt` and
`opp_followup_prompt` — found that every builder's text starts with a letter. A *later*
line starting with `/` does occur (the `resume.txt` fixture has one), which is why the
rule reads only the first non-whitespace character of the whole text and never a line.

**The browser type route is unchanged.** The operator typing into the session page's input
panel is a human at their own keyboard who may legitimately want `/compact`, and a test in
this spec asserts that route still delivers it. Spec 018 FR-006 says the API door's prompt
route is unchanged, so this decision **amends that FR** too, for this one refusal.

## D6 — The lock and the buffer (requirement 5)

`Prompt` takes the restart claim (`claimRestart`, non-blocking) immediately after
`lockSession`, refuses with `ErrSessionNotReady` when a revive or a continue already holds
it, and releases it on return.

Measured here, and therefore *not* new work in this spec:

- `lockSession` (`internal/session/input.go`) is already the per-session mutex shared by
  `Type`, `PressKey`, `Prompt`, `Compact`, `SetMode`, `Continue`, `Destroy` and the
  supervisor's Codex discovery. Two concurrent prompts to one session already serialise.
- `Exec.paste` (`internal/tmuxctl/exec.go`) already makes a fresh buffer name per paste
  via `newBufferName`, so two pastes cannot clobber one buffer. The fake records the
  names it was given (`nextBuffer`), so a test can assert they differ.

Both came out of the spec 018 and 019 reviews. What is new here is only the claim: a
revive or a continue is *typing a command line into the pane*, and a prompt pasted into
the middle of that line is neither a prompt nor a command. The claim is non-blocking on
purpose — a prompt that waited for a restart would be delivered into a session whose
conversation has since been replaced, which is worse than a refusal the caller can retry.

## D7 — `request_id` (requirement 6)

The prompt body gains one optional field, `request_id`: 1 to 32 characters of `[a-z0-9-]`.
A value outside that is `400`. A valid value is echoed in the `202` body and written as
`request_id` on the audit record. Absent means the field appears nowhere — not in the
response, not on the trail.

This **amends spec 001 FR-042** ("audit records carry no caller-supplied free text") for
this one field, and the bound is what makes the amendment safe to take: 32 characters of
`[a-z0-9-]` cannot carry prompt text, a sentence, a path, or a credential, and the
character class keeps it out of trouble in a JSONL record and in a log line. The
amendment is recorded in spec.md and in `specs/001-crswd-daemon-core/contracts/http-api.md`.

What it buys: lawnmower delivers a prompt and then reads the trail to find out what
happened to it. Without a correlator it matches on session ID and time, which is ambiguous
for exactly the case that matters — two deliveries to one session in one second.

**No length and no hash of the prompt**, here or anywhere else. The rule in
`docs/security.md` §3 stands unchanged: a length is a disclosure and a hash is a
disclosure of a guessable value.

## D8 — The registry gate (requirement 7) is deferred

Requirement 7 — consult Claude Code's `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` registry to decide
whether a session is ready — is **not built**, and the spec lists it under Out of scope
with this reason. It was a MAY in the design, not a MUST.

Evidence, all from the probe:

- Check 8 left open whether crswd can read `sessions/<pid>.json` at all under v2
  option B. No FR in spec 017 places that file in the cluster deployment, so a gate
  reading it would work on the VM and silently answer nothing in Kubernetes.
- Checks 3 and 9: the registry misses the trust dialog and misses a half-typed draft.
  So it does not answer the question the liveness gate (D2) answers, and a gate built on
  it would pass a session that cannot take a prompt.

A deferred MAY with a recorded reason is not an open question: **this is not a
NEEDS CLARIFICATION**, and nothing downstream waits on it.

## D9 — Out of scope

Named here so that a later iteration does not read one of these as missing work:

- **Opening a transcript.** The no-transcript rule holds (FR-025, recorded in
  `docs/security.md` as spec 013 FR-025); the bounded Codex exception (spec 019 D11) is
  that spec's and is not widened here.
- **Holding or calling an LLM.** This daemon delivers text; it does not author it.
- **A seventh API route.** The API door has six (measured here: the route switch in
  `internal/httpapi/server.go`, and six `## <VERB> <path>` headings in the contract).
  Every change in this spec lands on the existing prompt route.
- **Free text on the browser door beyond spec 018.** The session page's input panel is
  that spec's and keeps its behaviour, D5 included.
- **The startup lost-Enter window.** Probe check 1 found no check-then-Enter race after
  the first turn, and a lost Enter only inside roughly the first 5 s after a launch. That
  window is real and is not closed here.
- **The socket transport.** The probe's verdict was "flip to socket"; it binds the
  lm-steer-write milestone, not this one.
- **A new package under `internal/`.** Every change lands in `audit`, `httpapi`,
  `session` or `tmuxctl`.

## Not verified

- Whether Claude Code's registry file is reachable from a session pod (probe check 8,
  deferred with requirement 7 under D8).
- The exact width of the startup window in which an Enter can be lost; probe check 1
  bounds it at roughly 5 s and this spec does not depend on the number.
- Whether a `LivenessUnknown` pane can be running a harness that would swallow a paste.
  D2 delivers on unknown by spec 012 FR-006; no probe check contradicts it.

start a new session and it can use either Codex or Claude. I need it to have all the same
capabilities, functions, features, and stuff. … I don't think Codex has a remote control-capable

# Feature Specification: Prompt Route Safety

**Feature Branch**: `plan/lm-steer-crswd-018`

**Created**: 2026-10-14

**Status**: Draft (decisions recorded in [research.md](research.md) D1–D9)

**Depends on**: spec 018 (interactive input) and spec 019 (Codex runtime), both merged to `main`.

**Input**: `~/code/ai-lawnmower/docs/mcp-session-steering-design.md`, section (g) "Phase 3
detail", requirements 1 to 7. Evidence from the probe run in
`~/code/ai-lawnmower/ralph/plans/lm-steer-design/results.md`. Both documents live outside
this repository and are read, never edited.

## What this is

`POST /sessions/{id}/prompt` is the one route that delivers caller-authored text into a
running session, and lawnmower already drives it: `answer`, `resume`, the opp-lease batch
handoff and the opp follow-up all arrive here. Today the route pastes and presses Enter
with no question asked about whether anything is listening, which means the failure mode
is silent — text typed at a dead harness lands on a login shell, and text typed beside a
restart lands in the middle of a command line.

This spec closes those gaps on the route as it stands. It adds no route, no package, no
`Controller` method and no dependency; every change lands on the existing prompt route,
`internal/session`'s `Manager.Prompt`, the audit record and the `tmuxctl` fake.

Requirements 1 to 6 of the design are built. Requirement 7 is deferred with a recorded
reason (Out of scope, below). Every decision this spec rests on was taken before it was
written and is reproduced with its evidence in [research.md](research.md); none is
reopened here, and no open question remains in this document.

## Non-goals

- **Deciding readiness from Claude Code's session registry.** Requirement 7's
  `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` gate is deferred (research D8). See Out of scope.
- **Opening a transcript.** The no-transcript rule holds; spec 019 D11's bounded Codex
  exception is that spec's and is not widened.
- **Holding or calling an LLM.** This daemon delivers text; it does not author it.
- **A seventh API route.** The API door has six and keeps six.
- **Free text on the browser door beyond spec 018.** The session page's input panel keeps
  its behaviour exactly, including its acceptance of a leading `/`.
- **The startup window in which an Enter can be lost** (probe check 1), and **the socket
  transport** (the probe's own verdict, which binds the lm-steer-write milestone).

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - A prompt into a session whose harness has exited is refused (Priority: P1)

Lawnmower delivers an answer to a session whose Claude process exited some minutes ago.
The pane is a login shell. Today the text is pasted into that shell and Enter runs it as a
command line; the caller is told `delivered: true` and nothing anywhere records that the
conversation never saw it. Instead the daemon reads the pane's liveness, refuses, and says
so, having typed nothing.

**Why this priority**: it is the one failure in which a refused-looking success causes
execution the operator never asked for. Requirement 1 of the design.

**Independent Test**: with the fake controller's pane command set to something other than
the session's `@crswd-binary`, `Manager.Prompt` returns `ErrSessionNotReady`, and the fake
records no `load-buffer`, no `paste-buffer` and no `send-keys`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a running session whose pane command no longer matches `@crswd-binary`,
   **When** a prompt is delivered, **Then** it is refused with `ErrSessionNotReady` and
   nothing is typed into the pane.
2. **Given** a session whose liveness reads unknown — one started before `@crswd-binary`
   existed — **When** a prompt is delivered, **Then** it is delivered, exactly as spec 012
   FR-006 reads that value everywhere else.
3. **Given** a controller whose `List` fails, **When** a prompt is delivered, **Then** the
   call is an error and nothing is typed. The gate fails closed.
4. **Given** a session whose harness exits *between* the paste and the submit, **When** the
   second liveness read runs, **Then** the daemon sends `C-u`, sends no Enter, and answers
   `ErrSessionNotReady`, so the half-delivered text is cleared off the shell's line rather
   than executed by it.

---

### User Story 2 - A session that cannot take a prompt says so (Priority: P1)

Lawnmower delivers into a session the supervisor has marked `failed`. It gets a `409`
carrying `{"error":"session not ready"}`, which its own `deliver()` already reads as a
refusal, so it retries or escalates instead of believing the text arrived.

**Why this priority**: the caller's only existing signal is `delivered`, and a `500` is
indistinguishable from a host fault it should not retry. Requirement 2 of the design.

**Independent Test**: post a prompt for a `failed` session through the API door; the
response is `409` with that exact body, and the fake records no tmux command.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a session in state `failed`, **When** a prompt is delivered, **Then** the
   answer is `409` with body `{"error":"session not ready"}` and no tmux command ran.
2. **Given** any refusal that `ErrSessionNotReady` carries — failed state, stopped
   liveness, a held restart claim — **When** the caller reads the answer, **Then** it is the
   same `409` and the same body, and which gate refused is distinguishable only on the
   audit trail.
3. **Given** a session in state `dead`, **When** a prompt is delivered, **Then** the answer
   is the one it is today, unchanged: the resolver's uniform `404`.
4. **Given** a refused prompt, **When** the trail is read, **Then** the request's one audit
   record is a Deny whose reason is `session not ready` and which carries no prompt text.

---

### User Story 3 - A multi-line prompt arrives once, as one prompt (Priority: P1)

The opp-lease batch handoff is a dozen lines with blank lines in it. It must reach the
harness as one paste that one Enter submits, not as a dozen submissions of which the first
eleven are half-formed questions.

**Why this priority**: it is the shape of the traffic this route carries. Requirement 3 of
the design.

**Independent Test**: `Manager.Prompt` on a Claude session records `paste-buffer -p -d`
(bracketed) and then exactly one `send-keys Enter`; a two-line text records the same two
calls and no more.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a Claude session, **When** a prompt is delivered, **Then** it is pasted
   bracketed and submitted by one Enter.
2. **Given** a Codex session, **When** a prompt is delivered, **Then** it is pasted
   bracketed and submitted by one Enter, as spec 019 FR-006 already requires.
3. **Given** a prompt holding a newline, **When** it is delivered, **Then** it is not
   refused for holding one.
4. **Given** a Compact, **When** it is delivered, **Then** its paste is the harness-based
   one it is today and this spec changes nothing about it.

---

### User Story 4 - A prompt that would not be a prompt is refused (Priority: P2)

A caller's text begins with `/` or `!`. Delivered as-is it is a Claude Code slash command
or its shell escape, so a steering message silently becomes `/clear` and the conversation
it was steering is gone, with no error anywhere. The API door refuses it instead, before
anything is typed.

**Why this priority**: the damage is unbounded and invisible, but no current caller sends
such a text, so this is a guard rather than a fix. Requirement 4 of the design.

**Independent Test**: post `"/clear"` and `"  \n!rm -rf /"` to the API prompt route; each
is `400` with the uniform bad-request body and the fake records no tmux command. Post
`/compact` through the browser type route; it is delivered.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a text whose first character that is not a space, tab, CR or LF is `/` or `!`,
   **When** it is posted to the API prompt route, **Then** the answer is `400` with the
   uniform bad-request body and no tmux command ran.
2. **Given** a text whose first non-whitespace character is a letter but a **later line**
   starts with `/` — the `resume` fixture is one — **When** it is posted, **Then** it is
   delivered. The rule reads the first non-whitespace character of the whole text and never
   a line.
3. **Given** the session page's input panel, **When** the operator types `/compact` and
   submits, **Then** it is delivered. The operator is a human at their own keyboard and this
   refusal is not theirs.

---

### User Story 5 - A prompt never interleaves with a restart (Priority: P2)

A revive or a Continue is typing a command line into the pane. A prompt pasted into the
middle of that line is neither a prompt nor a command. The prompt is refused while the
restart holds its claim, and the caller may retry.

**Why this priority**: the window is narrow and the outcome is a corrupted command line on
a session running unsandboxed. Requirement 5 of the design.

**Independent Test**: hold `claimRestart` for a session, call `Manager.Prompt`, and get
`ErrSessionNotReady` with no tmux command recorded; release it and the same call delivers.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a revive or a Continue holding the session's restart claim, **When** a prompt
   is delivered, **Then** it is refused with `ErrSessionNotReady` and no tmux command ran.
2. **Given** a prompt that has taken the claim, **When** it returns — delivered or refused
   — **Then** the claim is released.
3. **Given** two prompts to one session at once, **When** both run, **Then** each paste
   uses a buffer name of its own and no paste is followed by the other call's Enter.

---

### User Story 6 - A caller can find its own delivery on the trail (Priority: P3)

Lawnmower delivers a prompt and then reads the audit trail to find out what happened to it.
It sends a correlator it chose; the `202` echoes it and the trail carries it, so two
deliveries to one session in one second are told apart by something other than the clock.

**Why this priority**: it is an observability affordance, not a safety gate, and the route
is correct without it. Requirement 6 of the design.

**Independent Test**: post a prompt with `"request_id":"abc-123"`; the `202` body carries
`"request_id":"abc-123"` and the request's one audit record carries the same value under
`request_id`. Post one with `"request_id":"AB C"`; it is `400` and no tmux command ran.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a body with a valid `request_id`, **When** the prompt is delivered, **Then**
   the `202` echoes it and the request's one audit record carries it.
2. **Given** a body with a `request_id` that is empty, longer than 32 characters, or holds a
   character outside `[a-z0-9-]`, **When** it is posted, **Then** the answer is `400` and no
   tmux command ran.

  carry prompt text, a sentence, a path or a credential. Prompt text, session output,
  credentials and the secret remain forbidden, asserted by test.
- **FR-019**: `specs/001-crswd-daemon-core/contracts/http-api.md` MUST record `request_id`,
  the `409` not-ready answer and the FR-009 refusal on the prompt route, and MUST still carry
  exactly six route headings.

### Bounds this spec keeps (restated so a change cannot drift past them)

- **FR-020**: No seventh API route. No new package under `internal/`. No new method on
  `tmuxctl.Controller`. No new dependency, and the root `go.sum` MUST stay absent.
- **FR-021**: Every new test MUST be table-driven, MUST call `t.Parallel()`, and MUST use the
  fake controller except in the one `//go:build tmux` file this spec adds.

### Out of scope

- **Requirement 7 — the session registry gate.** Consulting Claude Code's
  `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` to decide whether a session is ready is **not built**. It
  was a MAY in the design, and the probe gives two reasons to defer it: check 8 left open
  whether crswd can read that file at all under spec 017's v2 option B, so a gate reading it
  would work on the VM and answer nothing in Kubernetes; and checks 3 and 9 found the registry
  misses both the trust dialog and a half-typed draft, so it does not answer the question
  FR-001's liveness gate answers and would pass a session that cannot take a prompt. A
  deferred MAY with a recorded reason leaves no open question and nothing downstream waits on
  it (research D8).
- Everything under Non-goals above (research D9).

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

- **SC-001**: A test proves that a prompt into a session whose pane command does not match
  `@crswd-binary` is refused and that the fake recorded no `load-buffer`, no `paste-buffer`
  and no `send-keys`. It fails against the code before FR-001.
- **SC-002**: A test using the fake's `ExitAfterPaste` proves that a harness exiting between
  the paste and the submit yields a recorded `C-u`, no recorded Enter, and
  `ErrSessionNotReady`.
- **SC-003**: A test proves a `failed` session answers `409` with
  `{"error":"session not ready"}`, and that the request's audit record is a Deny reading
  `session not ready`.
- **SC-004**: A test proves a Claude session's prompt is pasted bracketed, for a one-line and
  a two-line text, and that `Compact`'s paste is unchanged.
- **SC-005**: A table test proves the FR-009 refusal for `/…`, `!…`, and the same two behind
  leading whitespace; proves delivery for a text whose first non-whitespace character is a
  letter and a later line starts with `/`; and proves the browser type route still delivers
  `/compact`.
- **SC-006**: A `-race` test with two goroutines prompting one session proves distinct buffer
  names and that no paste is separated from its own Enter.
- **SC-007**: A test proves a held restart claim refuses a prompt with no tmux command, and
  that the claim is free after a prompt returns.
- **SC-008**: Tests prove a valid `request_id` is echoed and audited, that each invalid shape
  is `400` with no tmux command, and that an absent one appears in neither the response nor
  the record. `internal/audit`'s leak test still passes unchanged.
- **SC-009**: A test posts each of the four lawnmower payload fixtures
  (`internal/httpapi/testdata/lawnmower/`) through the API prompt route and gets `202` with
  `delivered: true` — the traffic this route exists to carry still passes every gate added
  here.
- **SC-010**: A `//go:build tmux` test on a private `-L` socket proves that a pane sitting on
  `sh` with `@crswd-binary` of `claude` is refused and the pane stays empty, and that a
  two-line prompt into `cat` arrives once.
- **SC-011**: `go test ./...`, `go test -tags tmux ./...`, `go vet` on the default, `tmux` and
  `quickstart` builds, `gofmt -l .` and `golangci-lint run` are all green, and `go.sum` does
  not exist.

## Assumptions

- `@crswd-binary` is a usable liveness answer on the panes lawnmower drives. Probe check 13
  matched it against `pane_current_command` on 6 of 6 live panes, 3 of them under `rcq`.
- Lawnmower's `deliver()` treats any body carrying an `error` key as a refusal, so the `409`
  in FR-006 needs no change on that side.
- Every lawnmower prompt builder's text begins with a letter (grep of 10/14/26), so FR-009
  refuses none of today's traffic.
- `lockSession`, `claimRestart`/`releaseRestart` and `newBufferName` already exist and behave
  as research D6 records; this spec adds the claim to `Prompt` and asserts the other two.
- Spec 012 FR-006's reading of `LivenessUnknown` as alive — written on the
  `tmuxctl.Liveness` type itself and already relied on by `internal/session/supervisor.go` —
  continues to hold.
